Biker-Friendly Campsites Across the UK

Not all campsites welcome motorcyclists with open arms. Some treat bikes as second-class vehicles, shove them into awkward corners, or lack the facilities touring riders need. These campsites are different — they understand bikers, offer what we need, and sit on some of the best riding roads in Britain.

What Makes a Campsite "Biker-Friendly"?

  • Hard standing or firm ground: Nothing worse than a heavy touring bike sinking into soft grass. The best biker campsites offer hard standing or at least firm, well-drained pitches.
  • Secure parking: Ideally gated access, CCTV, or at minimum a designated motorcycle parking area within sight of reception.
  • Drying room: After a wet riding day, somewhere to hang waterproofs and boots to dry is invaluable.
  • Flexible arrival times: Motorcycle tourers don't always arrive by 3pm. Late check-in options matter.
  • Nearby riding roads: The best biker campsite is one surrounded by great biking roads.

Scotland

  • Applecross Campsite, Wester Ross: Perched at the end of the legendary Bealach na Bà pass. Basic facilities but the setting — looking across to Skye and Raasay — is extraordinary. Firm grass pitches. The Applecross Inn serves exceptional local seafood.
  • Loch Lomond Holiday Park, Balloch: Well-equipped site on the southern shore of Loch Lomond. Hard standings available. Gateway to the Trossachs and Glencoe riding.
  • Broomfield Holiday Park, Ullapool: Excellent base for the NC500 western section. Good facilities, walking distance to Ullapool for shops and restaurants.
  • Glenmore Campsite, Cairngorms: In the heart of the Cairngorms National Park. Surrounded by stunning mountain roads and ancient Caledonian pine forest.

England

  • Castlerigg Hall, Keswick, Lake District: Spectacular fell views, walking distance to Keswick, and surrounded by the Lake District's best biking roads. The Honister and Hardknott passes are day-ride distance.
  • Hooks House Farm, Whitby, North York Moors: Clifftop campsite near Whitby with views across Robin Hood's Bay. The North York Moors roads are superb for biking.
  • Fieldhead Campsite, Edale, Peak District: Small, friendly site in the heart of the Peak District. The Snake Pass, Cat and Fiddle, and Winnats Pass are all within easy reach.
  • South Penquite Farm, Bodmin Moor, Cornwall: Working farm campsite on Bodmin Moor. Perfectly placed for Cornish coastal rides and Dartmoor excursions.

Wales

  • Cae Du Campsite, Tywyn, Snowdonia: Small, well-maintained site within striking distance of all major Snowdonia passes including the Abergwesyn mountain road.
  • Trefalen Farm, Pembrokeshire: Clifftop camping above the Pembrokeshire Coast Path. The coastal roads are magnificent on a motorcycle.
  • Graig Wen, Dolgellau: Hillside campsite with panoramic views of the Mawddach Estuary and Cadair Idris. Some of Wales's best riding roads pass the door.
Tip: Call ahead and mention you're arriving by motorcycle. Most biker-friendly sites will save you a firm pitch and give you parking advice. A quick phone call makes all the difference.

Booking Tips for Motorcycle Tourers

  • Pre-book in peak season (June-August) — popular campsites fill up.
  • Ask about motorcycle-specific facilities when you book (hard standing, bike wash, secure parking).
  • Many campsites offer discount for motorcycle tourers — always ask.
  • Arrive before 6pm if possible — setting up camp in daylight is far easier.
  • If you're touring without booking, carry cash. Some smaller sites don't take cards.

A great campsite turns a good touring day into a perfect one. These sites understand riders and put you within arm's reach of Britain's finest roads. Pitch your tent, crack open a drink, and plan tomorrow's ride.

faq.a: The best sites offer hard standing or firm, well-drained ground so a heavy bike does not sink, secure parking with gated access or CCTV, a drying room for wet waterproofs and boots, flexible arrival times because tourers do not always arrive by 3pm, and above all a location surrounded by great riding roads.

Applecross Campsite sits at the end of the legendary Bealach na Ba pass with extraordinary views across to Skye and Raasay, and the Applecross Inn serves exceptional seafood. Broomfield Holiday Park in Ullapool is an excellent NC500 base, while Glenmore Campsite lies in the heart of the Cairngorms surrounded by mountain roads and ancient pine forest.

faq.q: What are good options in England and Wales?
faq.a: In England, Castlerigg Hall near Keswick offers fell views with the Honister and Hardknott passes at day-ride distance, and Fieldhead in Edale puts the Snake Pass, Cat and Fiddle and Winnats Pass within easy reach. In Wales, Cae Du near Tywyn reaches all the major Snowdonia passes, and Graig Wen near Dolgellau overlooks the Mawddach Estuary.

Yes. Call ahead and mention you are arriving by motorcycle. Most biker-friendly sites will save you a firm pitch and give you parking advice, and a quick phone call makes all the difference between a good pitch and a soft corner of a field. Ask specifically about hard standing, secure parking and a bike wash.

faq.q: Do I need to book and carry cash?
faq.a: Pre-book in peak season from June to August, as popular sites fill up, and arrive before 6pm so you can set up camp in daylight. If you are touring without booking, carry cash, because some smaller sites do not take cards. Many campsites also offer a discount for motorcycle tourers, so it is always worth asking.
